prompt: If $5 \le 2x + 1 \le 13$, what is the greatest possible value of $x$?
hint: Whatever you do, do it to all three parts at once.

hints.text: Whatever you do, do it to all three parts at once.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a shorter one: $3 \le x + 1 \le 7$. Subtract $1$ from all three parts to get $2 \le x \le 6$. Whatever you do, do it to every part at once.
Divide by $2$ throughout: $2 \le x \le 6$, so the greatest value is $6$.

learningObjective: Solve a compound inequality and read off an extreme value.
explanation: Divide all three parts by $2$: $2 \le x \le 6$.
The inequality is inclusive, so $x = 6$ is allowed and is the greatest possible value. Check: $2(6) + 1 = 13 \le 13$ ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Work only the end you need
steps: The question asks for the *greatest* $x$, which comes from the upper bound alone.
Half the work when only one end is requested — but read carefully, because "greatest" and "least" look alike under time pressure.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The least value, 2, is offered for anyone who solves correctly and then reads the question's direction backwards.
Underline greatest or least before solving. The compound inequality hands you both ends; the question wants exactly one.
